sources.citation: Huziwara, Keisuke (藤原敬介). 2013. カドゥー語音韻論 [Kadu phonology]. 東南アジア研究 51(1): 3-33. doi:10.20495/tak.51.1_3
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Not applicable: the article describes Kadu of Banmauk, Sagaing Division, Burma (Luish group; Glottolog kadu1254), not Loloish Kaduo. Glottolog's assignment to kadu1253 is an error.

sources.citation: van der Hulst, Harry & Rob Goedemans (eds.). 2010. A survey of word accentual patterns in the languages of the world, ch. 10 (Asia).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Kaduo appears only in the genealogical language index (BI-KA: Biyo, Kaduo); no stress entry or data for it.

sources.citation: Hansson, Inga-Lill. 1989. A comparison of Akha, Hani, Khatu and Pijo. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 12(1): 6-91.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Gives Khatu (=Kaduo, one Mojiang speaker) finals, initials and tones (High/Mid/Low, laryngealized Mid/Low; 'The low tone is in all of them slightly falling. Some differences in the tones may depend on sandhi rules, which remain to be worked out for Hani, Khatu, and Pijo', journal p. 8). Full-text scanned contains no mention of stress or accent; rest is PL correspondence sets and a 581-item wordlist.
